title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Your version catalog gets colours and fold arrows
summary: VS Code ships no TOML grammar, so gradle/libs.versions.toml opens in one colour with nothing to collapse. Kotlin Jump now colours it and folds it.

highlights.title: Colours for the version catalog
highlights.description: Table headers, aliases, version literals, coordinates and comments each get their own colour, and a version.ref target is coloured as a reference so an entry and the version it points at read as a pair.

highlights.title: Fold arrows on each table
highlights.description: Every table collapses to its header, and a bundle written over several lines collapses on its own.

sections.heading: Added
bullets: Colour and folding for any file named like a version catalog, so a TOML extension installed alongside keeps every other .toml file to itself.
The theme mapping for semantic tokens was declared for every language while all of it named Kotlin scopes. It is now declared for Kotlin only.
